stem: A pharmacy serving a long-term-care facility receives a faxed Schedule II prescription for an LTCF resident. The prescription is otherwise valid. Which federal rule is most relevant to whether the fax may serve as the original?

choices.text: The fax can serve as the original for the Schedule II prescription to the LTCF resident under the specific federal exception.
The exception applies only if the Schedule II drug is a narcotic.
The fax is never an original because LTCF status affects only partial filling.
The fax becomes valid only after seven days have elapsed.
The facility must convert the prescription to Schedule III before the fax can be used.

explanation.core_reasoning: A faxed Schedule II prescription for an LTCF resident may serve as the original when federal requirements are met.

choice_analysis.A: Federal law provides an LTCF fax-as-original exception.
choice_analysis.B: The LTCF exception is not limited to narcotics.
choice_analysis.C: LTCF status also matters to this fax rule.
choice_analysis.E: A facility cannot reclassify the drug.

related_facts: The exception is broader than the hospice narcotic exception with respect to narcotic status.
explanation.mpje_trap: Importing the narcotic limitation from the hospice fax exception.

reasoning_steps: Identify the patient as an LTCF resident
Apply the LTCF Schedule II fax exception
